newsitem.title: UK: Merrill's Lubash warns on Hungary social deficit.
newsitem.headline: Merrill's Lubash warns on Hungary social deficit.

text.p: Hungary's burgeoning social security fund deficit may delay a recovery in the country's economy until late 1997 or 1998, Merrill Lynch first vice president Dan Lubash warned in a note to investors.

"We believe that the latest estimate of 65 billion forints for the deficit is unlikely to be the final figure and that an increased deficit may have to be financed from additional revenue sources," Lubash said.

Hungary said earlier this month it plans to cut budget expenditures by 10 billion forints to meet an International Monetary Fund-agreed target of a budget deficit of 4.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The deficit of the social security funds, including pension and health care, soared to 56 billion forints by the end of August, compared with a 17.8 billion forint target for 1996.
In 1996, Merrill forecasts economic growth of just 0.5 percent of GDP and sees a consolidated budget deficit of 5.5 percent of GDP. In 1997, it believes economic growth will be less than 2.0 percent.
As a result, Merrill is overweighting companies in the equity market that have international expsoure through export earnings rather than those dependent on a stagnant local economy.
Merrill reiterated its buy on drugs companies Gedeon Richter, 55 percent of whose earnings are from overseas, and Egis with 40 percent of its earnings from overseas.
